title: Approvals needed for a data centre in India: permits, NOCs and who issues them
summary: Approvals for a data centre in India: no single licence, but EC at 20,000 sq m or more, CTE and CTO, groundwater, airport height and fire NOCs, diesel licence.

title: How to set up a data centre in India: from entity to energisation (2026)

title: Data centre cost per MW in India: ₹35 to 75 crore to build, plus land (2026)

title: Data centre site due diligence in India: the feasibility checklist (2026)
summary: Data centre site due diligence in India: power evidence, title, groundwater (730 of 6,762 units over-exploited), seismic zone, flood history and AAI height limits.

title: Data centre land in India: acres per MW, land prices and powered land (2026)
summary: Data centre land in India costs ₹3 to 60 crore per acre and about half an acre per MW on Anarock’s 2026 bands. Recent deals, parks, FAR rules and powered land.

title: Seismic zones, flood and cyclone risk for data centres in India (2026)
summary: Seismic zones of Indian data centre cities under IS 1893 (Delhi IV; Mumbai and Chennai III), the withdrawn Zone VI map, record floods, cyclones and CRZ limits.

title: Water for data centres in India: groundwater NOC, water stress and state rules
summary: Data centres in India need a CGWA or state NOC to draw groundwater. Anarock puts use at about 25.5 million litres per MW a year. Water-stressed cities, state rules.

title: Power for data centres in India: grid supply, open access and tariffs by state
summary: How data centres in India buy power: discom supply, green open access from 100 kW, captive plants, and state tariffs such as Tamil Nadu’s ₹7.50/kWh plus ₹608/kVA.

title: Data centre grid connection in India: voltage by load, dual grid and GNA (2026)
summary: Data centre grid connection in India: supply moves to 110, 132 or 220 kV above about 10 MVA, who pays for lines and bays, and direct inter-state access from 50 MW.

title: Green energy open access for data centres in India: rules, banking and ISTS (2026)
summary: Green energy open access for data centres in India: 100 kW eligibility, 15-day deemed approval, monthly banking, the ISTS waiver phase-out to 2028 and captive rules.

title: Open access charges by state in India: cross subsidy surcharge and wheeling (2026)
summary: Open access charges for data centres in India: cross subsidy surcharge, additional surcharge, wheeling, banking, the 2022 green caps and state waivers up to 100%.

title: India data centre power demand to 2032: what CEA and the government project
summary: India data centre power demand: CEA projects about 17 GW by 2031-32, other official figures range from 13.56 GW to 26.3 GW, and how that compares with peak demand.

title: Power study for a data centre site in India: load flow and N-1 against the grid
summary: Power study for a data centre site in India: load flow and N-1 tests to state grid code criteria, such as Maharashtra’s 500 MVA norm for a 220 kV substation.

title: Diesel generator rules for data centres in India: CPCB IV, consents and PESO (2026)
summary: Diesel generator rules for data centres in India: CPCB IV for gensets up to 800 kW, Orange category from 1 MVA on liquid fuel, PESO licence above 25,000 litres.

title: National data centre policy in India: the 2020 draft and what applies now (2026)
summary: India has no notified national data centre policy as of November 2026: MeitY's 2020 draft was never notified and talks reopened in August 2025. What applies instead.

title: Data centre incentives in India: infrastructure status, tax holiday and SEZs (2026)
summary: Central data centre incentives in India: infrastructure status for 5 MW+ IT load since October 2022, a tax holiday to 2047 for cloud services, FDI and SEZ rules.

title: DPDP Act and data localisation: what it means for data centres in India (2026)
summary: India's DPDP Act 2023 does not require blanket data localisation, but RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, CERT-In and telecom rules do. What each rule means for data centres.

title: Data centre policy in India: state data centre policies compared (2026)
summary: State data centre policies in India compared: 11 states had policies in force in September 2026 (Invest India). Subsidy, power tariff and stamp duty by state.

title: Uttar Pradesh data centre policy 2026: parks, capital subsidy and power incentives
summary: Uttar Pradesh Data Centre Policy 2026: up to ₹50 crore interest subsidy for parks, 7% capital subsidy up to ₹20 crore for units, 10-year electricity duty exemption.

title: Maharashtra data centre policy 2026: green data centre parks and IT/ITES incentives
summary: Maharashtra covers data centres in its IT/ITES Policy 2023 and a green parks policy expanded to 20 parks in June 2026, with a 20-year electricity duty exemption.

title: Tamil Nadu data centre policy: the 2021 policy, incentives and status (2026)
summary: Tamil Nadu Data Centre Policy 2021: ₹500 crore minimum and 30% renewable power, for data centres incorporated by 31 March 2026. No successor found by November 2026.

title: Telangana data centre policy: the 2016 policy, incentives and Hyderabad (2026)
summary: Telangana’s Data Centres Policy 2016 is the latest we found as of November 2026. The state targets 5 GW by 2029; Hyderabad had 151 MW live in mid-2026.

title: Gujarat data centre policy 2026-29: 150 MW threshold and ₹1 per unit subsidy
summary: Viksit Gujarat Data Centre Policy 2026-29: 150 MW minimum IT load, 51% renewable power, ₹1 per unit for 20 years and a 7.5 GW target, launched 9 July 2026.

title: Karnataka data centre policy 2026-31: incentives, water rules and the 2022 policy
summary: Karnataka Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31, approved in September 2026: ₹1,300.45 crore budget, 1 GW target and up to ₹20 crore for a PUE of 1.00 to 1.20.

title: Andhra Pradesh data centre policy 4.0 (2024-29): incentives and mega projects
summary: Andhra Pradesh data centre policy 4.0 (2024-29): SGST refund or a 10% capital subsidy; four projects cleared in 2026 with ₹2.83 lakh crore of proposed investment.

title: Haryana data centre policy 2026: capex and opex support and the 2022 policy
summary: Haryana Data Centre Policy 2026 (27 May 2026): hyperscale data centres above 10 MW get 20% capex support up to ₹25 crore and 50% opex support up to ₹8 crore a year.

title: Rajasthan data centre policy 2025: investment target, status and official text
summary: Rajasthan’s Data Centre Policy 2025 aims to attract about ₹20,000 crore of data centre investment over five years, the Chief Minister said in April 2025.

title: Odisha data centre policy 2022: capital subsidy, power subsidy and SGST refund
summary: Odisha's State Data Centre Policy 2022 gives a 20% capital subsidy up to ₹25 crore, a 30% power bill subsidy for five years and 100% net SGST reimbursement.

title: West Bengal data centre policy 2021: incentives, essential services and status
summary: West Bengal's Data Centre Policy 2021 gave stamp duty and electricity duty relief and essential services status; its five-year term ended around September 2026.

title: Madhya Pradesh data centre policy: IT, ITeS and ESDM Policy 2023 incentives (2026)
summary: We found no standalone Madhya Pradesh data centre policy; its IT, ITeS and ESDM Policy 2023 gives anchor data centres 25% capex support up to ₹125 crore each.

title: Data centres in Mumbai and Navi Mumbai: capacity, sub-markets and power (2026)

title: Data centres in Chennai: capacity, Ambattur, Siruseri and flood risk (2026)

title: Data centres in Hyderabad: capacity, hyperscalers and power (2026)
summary: Hyderabad had 151 MW of operational data centre capacity in H1 2026 and India’s second-largest pipeline after Mumbai, with AWS and Microsoft cloud regions.

title: Data centres in Noida and Delhi NCR: Greater Noida, YEIDA and Gurugram (2026)

title: Data centres in Bengaluru: capacity, Whitefield, Hoskote and water (2026)
summary: Bengaluru had 162 MW of operational data centre capacity in H1 2026 (Cushman & Wakefield), mostly in Whitefield, with 28% vacancy. Water is the binding constraint.

title: Data centres in Pune: capacity, Hinjewadi, PBD North and power (2026)
summary: Pune had 133 MW of operational data centre capacity in H1 2026, per Cushman & Wakefield, mostly in PBD North and Hinjewadi. Sub-markets, power, policy and risks.

title: Data centres in Visakhapatnam: Google’s AI hub, gigawatt campuses and risks (2026)

title: Data centres in Gujarat: Jamnagar, GIFT City, Ahmedabad and Dholera (2026)

title: Data centres in Kolkata and East India: New Town, Salt Lake and Bhubaneswar (2026)
summary: Kolkata had 22 MW of operational data centre capacity in H1 2026, mostly in New Town, per Cushman & Wakefield. West Bengal’s 2021 policy term ran to September 2026.

title: Data centre companies in India: the largest operators and recent deals (2026)

title: Mumbai vs Chennai vs Hyderabad for data centres: power, policy and risk (2026)
summary: Mumbai had 890 MW of live data centre capacity in H1 2026, Chennai 214 MW and Hyderabad 151 MW. Power, policy, rents, flood and seismic risk compared.

title: India vs Singapore vs Johor for data centres: power, policy and cost (2026)

title: AI data centres in India: gigawatt campuses, IndiaAI GPUs and power (2026)
